newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland voters pass operating levy for schools.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland voters pass operating levy for schools.

text.p: Cleveland voters finally said yes Tuesday to a hike in the operating millage levy for the Cleveland Public Schools.
Unofficial results from Tuesday's voting showed 72,735 votes in favor of the 13.5 mill property tax hike and 61,345 against, according to Rick Ellis, communications director for the school district.

The last levy increase passed by voters for the school system was in 1983. Strained finances led Ohio Department of Education to take control of the schools in March 1995. Last month, Ohio Auditor Jim Petro declared a fiscal emergency for the district.
The 13.5 mill property tax hike is expected to raise $67.5 million a year.
School officials have said the levy was needed to improve services and to start paying off about $87 million of the school system's operating debt.
In August, a U.S. District Court Judge in Cleveland ordered the proposed operating levy hike to be placed on the ballot after the Cleveland school board rejected the move.
The levy proposal was endorsed by Ohio Gov. George Voinovich and Cleveland Mayor Michael White.
